properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued July 31 at 10:01PM CDT until July 31 at 10:30PM CDT by NWS Lubbock TX
properties.description:
At 1001 PM CDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 7 miles northeast of Plainview to 5 miles west of
Lehman, moving southeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...West Texas Mesonet.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Lubbock, Plainview, Levelland, Littlefield, Slaton, Floydada,
Abernathy, Hale Center, Olton, Morton, Crosbyton, Plains, Wolfforth,
Shallowater, Idalou, Ralls, Lockney, Sundown, Petersburg, and
Lorenzo.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.headline: Tornado Warning issued July 31 at 10:01PM CDT until July 31 at 10:30PM CDT by NWS St Louis MO
properties.description:
At 1001 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located over Farmington, moving east at 35 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is
likely.

Locations impacted include...
Desloge, Park Hills, Doe Run, Leadington, Farmington, Knob Lick,
Libertyville, Mine La Motte, Weingarten, Coffman, Womac, River Aux
Vases, Minnith and St. Mary.

This includes the following State Parks...
St. Joe State Park, Hawn State Park and Missouri Mines Historic Site.

This includes Interstate 55 in Missouri between exits 141 and 143.
properties.instruction:
Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built building
away from windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a
vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself
from flying debris.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 31 at 6:09PM MDT until July 31 at 9:15PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Dona Ana County in south central New Mexico...

* Until 915 PM MDT.

* At 609 PM MDT, Slow moving thunderstorms have spread closer to
Interstate 10, just south of Las Cruces. Torrential rainfall rates
over 2 inches per hour have been observed.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of arroyos, urban areas, highways,
streets and underpasses as well as other poor drainage
and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Las Cruces, Mesquite and San Pablo.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 31 at 9:52PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Tilden, Three Rivers...Major
flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 39.2 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 39.0
feet on 10/21/2013.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 31 at 9:29PM CDT until August 1 at 5:00AM CDT by NWS St Louis MO
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in St Louis has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Missouri...

Meramec River near Steelville.

River forecasts are based on observed precipitation and forecast
precipitation for the next 24 hours.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast due to heavy rain.

* WHERE...Meramec River near Steelville.

* WHEN...From this evening to late tonight.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:15 PM CDT Friday the stage was 10.2 feet.
- Forecast...No forecast is available for this location.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Rainfall heavier than forecast could cause river levels to rise even
higher than predicted. The National Weather Service will monitor this
developing situation and issue follow up statements as conditions
change.

This product, along with additional weather and stream information,
is available at https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/lsx

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 31 at 8:50PM CDT until July 31 at 11:45PM CDT by NWS St Louis MO
properties.description:
FFWLSX

The National Weather Service in St Louis has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northern Crawford County in east central Missouri...
Northern Washington County in east central Missouri...

* Until 1145 PM CDT.

* At 850 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 3.5 inches of rain
have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour.
Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sullivan, Cuba, Bourbon, Anthonies Mill, Leasburg, Richwoods, Old
Mines, St. Cloud and Oak Hill.

This includes the following State Parks...
Washington State Park and Onondaga Cave State Park.

This includes Interstate 44 in Missouri between exits 203 and 218.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.
